scientific_integrity: The theorem is presented as a new reduct-fixed classification derived from the published irregular-successor family plus standard first-order locality. The unrestricted definitional-equivalence problem is explicitly left open here; no independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The classification fixes the common {0,suc} reduct. It does not classify arbitrary definitional equivalences that may redefine or rename the successor skeleton. The radius-one six-rule statement assumes both forward and inverse eventual rules have radius one.
title: Reversible block codes classify successor-reduct definitional equivalence in the irregular T(S) family
